analysis: Reviewed the supplied changes: documentation in docs/developer/test.md (the visible head text at lines 2303-3108, plus the patch excerpt for date bump, CI runner-routing wording near lines 1243-1247 and routed-job lane description near 1807-1810) and scripts/test-ci-component-paths.py (lines 277-296). Together they are test-documentation and CI-structure assertion changes. They touch no provider runtime code, no coordinator-to-provider wire contract, no keys, attestation, App Attest authorization, or prefix-cache storage. The visible test.md content describes existing test suites, including tenant prefix partition checks and SSD prefix record encoding checks. It does not change the T-041 posture: TTL, HMAC lookup tags and salt scoping. The text states that the synthetic checks are not hardware or tenant-isolation qualification, which is consistent with the threat model's limits. The Python test now asserts that CI lane jobs declare 'needs: [changes, route]', in addition to the existing 'if' guards on the classifier outputs. Whether the workflows in .github/workflows actually match these assertions is not visible here, and the workflow files are not in the supplied batch. The change only affects whether the CI self-test passes. The wording change from 'literal Blacksmith runners' to a routed runner plane for macOS jobs is a CI infrastructure change. The runner-routing plane, its fork-PR and label handling, and its permissions are documented elsewhere (build.md#ci-runner-routing), outside this batch. A later pass could confirm that the workflow changes keep read-only permissions and that fork PRs cannot route onto privileged self-hosted runners. No concrete security regression is visible in these units.
